Her question, and how the app answers it

Her question is simple; a trustworthy answer is not

  • Her question

    “Which product categories generate the most revenue?”

    She knows the business, not SQL; the data sits in an 11-table database.

  • Her options today

    Wait about three days for an analyst, or weeks for a curated tool to be set up.

    Or learn the schema and SQL herself.

  • What she needs

    An answer today, the SQL behind it so she can check it, and her data never changed.

One question’s path: one model call, two gates in code

Yellow is the model; teal is enforced in code.

The 21 % trap: why she needs the SQL

“Which product categories generate the most revenue?”

The SQL, and what “completed revenue” adds
SELECT category, SUM(unit_price * quantity
+ * (1 - discount_pct)
FROM order_items JOIN products ...
+ JOIN orders ...
+ WHERE order_status = 'Completed'
GROUP BY category
All orders, list price173,366
Completed, discounted136,98421 % lower

Electronics revenue: all 220 orders, or the 179 completed ones after discounts. Neither is wrong: the SQL shows the choice, and she decides.
